metadata.title: Shai-Hulud: the self-replicating worm returns via the software supply chain

notes: Ported from bubble-map #235 and enriched with the affected assets, known attack vectors, and mitigation routes as first-class nodes. The modern mutation of the worm: not email (ILOVEYOU) or SMB (EternalBlue) but package registries + CI/CD + AI coding agents - where trust and automation now concentrate. Mitigations are graded; note the arms race where Mini forges the very provenance attestation meant to stop it.

entities.name: Shai_Hulud
entities.notes: First wave detected 2025-09-16: ~187 npm packages compromised (incl. several tied to CrowdStrike). Self-replicating: steals npm token, injects an install hook into the victim's other packages, republishes an incremented patch, repeats. Harvests secrets with TruffleHog and exfiltrates to attacker-created PUBLIC GitHub repos; registers victims as self-hosted GitHub Actions runners for persistence.

entities.name: Shai_Hulud_V2
entities.notes: 'Sha1-Hulud: The Second Coming'. Second wave 2025-11-21..24: 700+ packages, 27,000+ malicious repos, ~14,000 secrets across 487 orgs (ranges vary by vendor). Escalation: runs during PRE-install (not post-install), uses the Bun runtime, and carries a DESTRUCTIVE dead-man payload (wipes home directory if it cannot exfiltrate).

entities.name: Mini_Shai_Hulud
entities.notes: 4th-generation variant, active since late Apr-2026, most destructive in the 2026-05-11 wave; actor self-labeled 'TeamPCP'. New tricks: PROVENANCE-ATTESTATION FORGERY and AI-CODING-AGENT persistence - deliberately targeting the AI-developer supply chain (tools with elevated filesystem access).

entities.name: GitHub
entities.notes: Microsoft-owned. In this campaign it is simultaneously the exfiltration surface (attacker-created public repos), the propagation surface (Actions runners), and the host of the compromised CI/CD.

entities.name: ctrl_tinycolor
entities.notes: @ctrl/tinycolor - a widely-depended-on npm color utility, among the patient-zero packages of the first wave. Illustrates blast radius: one small transitive dependency reaches thousands of downstream builds.

entities.name: CICD_Pipeline
entities.notes: GitHub Actions / CI runners. Both a victim (secrets in env, build access) and the propagation surface: the worm registers victim machines as self-hosted runners for persistence and re-execution.

entities.name: Cloud_Credentials
entities.notes: npm/GitHub PATs and AWS/GCP/Azure keys harvested from developer machines and CI env. ~14,000 secrets exfiltrated in the V2 wave; dumped to public GitHub repos for anyone to reuse.

entities.name: Npm_Maintainer_Account
entities.notes: The registry publisher account. Initial access to the first wave is attributed to phishing that harvested maintainer npm tokens (fake 'npmjs support' / lookalike domains). One stolen token = publish rights across all that maintainer's packages.

entities.name: AI_Coding_Agent
entities.notes: AI dev tools/agents with elevated filesystem + token access. Mini Shai-Hulud specifically targets this tier - trust + automation concentrated in a component that reads secrets and writes code.

entities.name: NPM_Lifecycle_Hooks
entities.notes: VECTOR: npm's pre/post-install lifecycle scripts run arbitrary code at `npm install` time. The worm injects an install hook into every package it can publish - the mechanism of both infection and self-replication. V2 moved to PRE-install to fire earlier.

entities.name: Maintainer_Phishing
entities.notes: VECTOR (initial access): credential-phishing of package maintainers via lookalike registry domains to steal npm publish tokens - the human foothold that seeds the automated spread.

entities.name: TruffleHog_Weaponized
entities.notes: VECTOR (collection): the worm bundles TruffleHog - a legitimate secret-scanning tool - to sweep the victim host/repo for tokens and cloud keys. Dual-use: the same scanner defenders run to find leaked secrets.

entities.name: CICD_Runner_Persistence
entities.notes: VECTOR (persistence): registers the victim as a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner, giving the attacker durable code execution inside the CI environment that survives the initial package removal.

entities.name: Provenance_Forgery
entities.notes: VECTOR (defense evasion): Mini forges npm provenance/attestation metadata so a poisoned package appears to have a trustworthy build origin - defeating the exact control introduced to stop supply-chain tampering.

entities.name: Disable_Install_Scripts
entities.notes: MITIGATION: install with lifecycle scripts disabled (`npm ci --ignore-scripts`, or `ignore-scripts=true`) so a poisoned package cannot execute on install. Directly neutralizes the primary infection mechanism.

entities.name: Trusted_Publishing_OIDC
entities.notes: MITIGATION: publish via short-lived OIDC 'trusted publishing' + granular/expiring tokens instead of long-lived PATs; enforce 2FA/passkeys on registry accounts. Removes the reusable-token loot the worm needs to republish.

entities.name: Dependency_Pinning_Cooldown
entities.notes: MITIGATION: pin exact versions via lockfile + integrity hashes and quarantine brand-new releases for a cooldown window - so a malicious patch bump is not pulled the moment it is published.

entities.name: NPM_Provenance_Attestation
entities.notes: MITIGATION (partially defeated): sigstore-backed npm provenance ties a package to its source + build. Strong against blind tampering - but Mini's forgery shows attestation is only as good as the trust in the signing path.

entities.name: Ephemeral_CI_LeastPriv
entities.notes: MITIGATION: ephemeral, isolated CI runners with least-privilege scoped secrets and egress filtering - so a compromised build cannot persist as a runner, read every secret, or phone home to GitHub-hosted drops.

entities.name: Secret_Rotation_Scanning
entities.notes: MITIGATION (response): continuous secret scanning + fast rotation. Because dumped secrets are public immediately, detection-to-rotation time is the whole game post-compromise.

edges.instrument: several CrowdStrike-tied packages in first wave
pre-install hook, Bun runtime, destructive payload

edges.notes: Arms race: the mitigation is only as strong as trust in the signing path.

edges.instrument: isolated runners + scoped secrets + egress filtering
scan + fast rotation (public dumps are immediate)
